constitutional_basis: Article XXIX — a failed embodiment (implementation) cannot kill the invention unless the design space is exhausted or an invariant proof shows impossibility. A bad geometry implementation does not automatically kill the scientific idea; an invalid geometry cannot be presented as manufacturing-ready. This record separates the three layers explicitly and machine-checkably.

scientific_concept.statement: A passive, valve-free dual-lumen drainage architecture in which a low-conductance floor lumen maintains a minimum drainage rate when the primary lumen is obstructed, providing an intrinsic safety floor against over-drainage/under-drainage failure of a CSF shunt's distal catheter.
scientific_concept.status: MECHANISM_SUPPORTED (4 governing equations, 10 design inputs, 5 failure modes, 5 external evidence items in the frozen dossier); PROBLEM EXISTENCE is itself recorded as partially unknown (clinical benefit magnitude UNKNOWN until trial)
scientific_concept.kill_condition: Common-cause obstruction affecting both primary and floor lumens equally (recorded critical unknown); clinical irrelevance of the maintained minimum flow (Q_min unknown)

engineering_architecture.statement: Extruded dual-lumen silicone catheter: primary lumen (1.1 mm) + eccentric floor lumen (0.6 mm) at 1.0 mm offset in a 3.0 mm OD body, 100 mm length; G_floor/G_primary = (d_floor/d_primary)^4 (Poiseuille, MODELLED).
engineering_architecture.status: ENGINEERING_DEFINED; parametric template tpl:P07_drainage_floor_dual_lumen:v1 with measured-on-built-solid constraints (min wall >= 0.15 mm, floor conductance split >= 0)
